title: pulsed-stream-handshake-and-action-layers-prd-wip
summary: Sketch PRD for a low-latency 'pulsed streaming' protocol and a layered action-output contract that improves tool-calling ergonomics for mobile and thin clients while preserving structured-output guarantees.
problem_statement: Existing streaming SDKs either send continuous character deltas (low overhead but noisy for tool routing) or large chunked frames (good for tools, bad for tail latency). Mobile and embedded clients suffer from unpredictable bursts and fragile tool handshakes. Teams building tool-enabled hosted API integrations need: (1) predictable tail latency across varying network conditions, (2) clearly typed action frames that can be processed incrementally, and (3) ergonomic SDK surface for resuming and reconciling partial outputs.
goals: Define a pulsed streaming transport that emits compact "pulses" (micro-batches) at configurable cadence to bound tail latency
Design an action-layer contract (ActionFrame v1) that decouples token streaming from tool invocation semantics
Propose SDK ergonomics (JS + mobile clients) for handshake, resumability, and partial validation
Provide structured-output examples and migration guidance for existing customers
Outline rollout plan with toggles, telemetry and backward compatibility
non_goals: Do not attempt to replace binary streaming transports (grpc/rtp) in this PRD
No model-side changes beyond annotated tokens and frame markers
Not covering enterprise-only Dedicated routing or private on-prem installation details
user_stories: As a mobile app developer I want consistent per-response tail latency so my UI spinner stops reliably
As a backend integrator I want action frames that can be committed or rolled back atomically so tool side-effects are safe
As SDK maintainer I want a small ergonomic surface for reconnect/resume so we avoid user confusion on flaky networks
As product manager I want telemetry hooks for pulse timing, action-failure rates, and resume success so we can set SLOs
requirements: REQ-1: Pulsed stream must bound maximum inter-pulse time configurable per-route (defaults: 50ms, 200ms, 500ms)
REQ-2: ActionFrame v1 must include typed header, stable id, optional preflight metadata, and commit/abort markers
REQ-3: SDK resume token must allow deterministic rehydration without double-invoking idempotent tool effects
REQ-4: Structured-output must be serializable as line-delimited JSON-LD fragments to allow incremental validation
REQ-5: Backward compat mode: server must accept legacy streaming clients and emit full frames on demand
api_surface_notes: We propose a small extension to the existing streaming response envelope: add two top-level frame types: 'pulse' and 'action-frame'. A 'pulse' packages 1..N tokens plus optional checkpoints; an 'action-frame' carries typed tool metadata and explicit commit/abort. Client can request pulse cadence via a request hint header 'X-Pulse-Cadence-ms'.
sdk_changes: JS SDK: add StreamController that exposes onPulse(callback) and onActionFrame(callback)
Mobile SDKs: lightweight reassembly util that accepts pulses and emits full transcripts or partial action objects
Client token semantics: new resume_token returned after each committed action-frame; SDK must surface safeResume(resume_token) helper
Validation helpers: incremental schema validator for structured fragments included in SDK
streaming_protocol_sketch: Pulse = {pulse_id, sequence_start, sequence_end, tokens[], optional checkpoint_meta}. ActionFrame = {action_id, action_type, payload_schema, preflight, commit_marker?, abort_marker?}. Example sequence (human readable): PULSE(toks 1..12) -> PULSE(toks 13..24 + checkpoint) -> ACTION_FRAME(preflight metadata) -> PULSE(action result tokens) -> ACTION_FRAME(commit_marker). The server can flush a full action-frame result in a single pulse if latency budget allows.
tool_call_contract: Tool calls are modeled as side-effectable ActionFrames. Preflight includes arguments and expected idempotency flags (none | safe-repeat | unique). The server holds off committing an action until the model emits the commit_marker; SDKs treat commit as the durable acknowledgement. If connection drops before commit, resume flow asks server for incomplete action_ids and either replay or abort based on idempotency flag.
telemetry_and_slo: Emit pulse_latency_histogram, pulses_per_response, action_commit_latency, resume_success_rate. SLO targets: p95 pulse latency < configured cadence + 10ms; action_commit p99 < 800ms for small actions. Rollout must include server-side adaptive cadence when p95 > configured to keep tail bounded.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: internal dogfood route behind feature flag for 2 teams (mobile chat, customer-success automation). Phase 1: opt-in beta for customers (beta flag in console) with telemetry sampling. Phase 2: gradual default enable for new routes with server-side adaptive cadence. Provide migration path: SDKs accept a 'compat_mode' that requests full frame flushing instead of pulses.
security_considerations: ActionFrame preflight may contain URLs or tokens—treat as sensitive metadata. Server must redact sensitive fields in logs by default and provide schema-driven allowlist for downstream tooling. Resume tokens must be HMAC-signed and short-lived. If an action is marked 'unique', server must prevent duplicate commit across resumes.
open_questions: Q1: What default cadence is best for mixed mobile/desktop traffic? (50ms gives best latency but increases overhead)
Q2: How to expose action idempotency flags in a backwards-compatible way to older models?
Q3: Do we need a server-side compensating action system for aborted/partial commits?
Q4: SDK ergonomics for multi-tab web apps (who owns resume token?)
next_steps: Prototype Pulse encoder/decoder in JS SDK (2 engineer-weeks)
Add action-frame support to streaming runtime (3 engineer-weeks)
Create dogfood dashboard widgets for pulse and commit telemetry (1 engineer-week)
Design migration docs and example integrations for customer-facing SDK samples (PM + DevRel)
